summary: Wallowa-Whitman NF site in Baker County: a 1939 cupola on a warehouse roof, a 19-foot pole platform added in 1942, abandoned in 1963 and gone.

facts.design: cupola built on a roof warehouse (1939); a 19-foot pole platform added in 1942
facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1963; the register lists it as gone

events.note: A cupola on a roof warehouse at the site
A 19-foot pole platform added to the site
Lookout abandoned; the register lists it as gone

evidence.supports: about 21 miles northwest of Baker City
cupola built on a roof warehouse at the site in 1939
evidence.quote: A cupola was built on a roof warehouse on the site in 1939.

evidence.supports: 1936-dated panoramic photo caption on the register page

evidence.quote: In 1942 a 19 foot pole platform was added to the site.
The lookout was abandoned in 1963 and is gone.

evidence.supports: administered by the U.S. Forest Service

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1939 as the build year, but its own photo caption is dated 1936. The page does not explain the difference, so the story reports both without choosing one.

sources.title: North Powder Lookout Site (Former Fire Lookout Sites register)

notes_for_editor: Two thin pages from the same register family. The 1936 photo caption predates the 1939 build date and is unexplained. The 1939 structure is a cupola on a warehouse roof, not clearly a platform, so the brief's kind of platform fits the 1942 addition better. A ranger roll call (ppolinks.com PDF) surfaced in search lists district rangers, not lookout staffing, so it was not used. No source describes the site today.
